Lessons.Title: Zeros of Polynomial Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: Original source learning goals: evaluate a polynomial via remainder theorem, apply factor theorem and Rational Zero Theorem, find real/complex roots, construct factors, analyze Descartes sign changes and solve polynomial volume models.
The Remainder Theorem says division by x−k leaves p(k); the Factor Theorem specializes this to zero remainder. Rational roots must be tested, not assumed.
The Rational Zero Theorem gives possible fractions ±(factor of constant)/(factor of leading coefficient), reduced to lowest terms.
Nonreal zeros of real-coefficient polynomials occur in conjugate pairs. All n complex roots of degree n are counted with multiplicity.
Descartes' Rule of Signs restricts possible positive/negative real zero counts but does not identify roots; explicitly test candidates.
Contextual models such as cubic volume require rejecting nonpositive lengths or other impossible roots.
Independent Edulytics cool-down: (a) Find remainder of x³−2x²+5x−4 on division by x−1. (b) Factor x³−6x²+11x−6. (c) Construct monic polynomial with roots 2,±i.
Independent Try It 1 — Remainder at negative input. Find remainder of p(x)=x³−4x²+x+7 divided by x+2.
Independent Try It 2 — Factor theorem with known root. Find zeros of p(x)=x³−5x²+2x+8 given x−2 is a factor.
Independent Try It 3 — Rational zero possibilities. List possible rational zeros of 3x³−4x²−7x+2.
Independent Try It 4 — Find real and complex zeros. Solve p(x)=x³−x²+9x−9.
Independent Try It 5 — Real coefficients conjugate pair. Build monic cubic with zeros −2,3i,−3i.
Independent Try It 6 — Descartes sign possibilities. For p(x)=x⁴−2x³−x²+4x−4, give allowed positive and negative root counts.
Independent Try It 7 — Box model polynomial dimensions. A box height h, width h+1, length 2h+1 has volume30 cubic units. Find positive h and dimensions.

KeyConcepts.Title: Remainder Theorem
KeyConcepts.Definition: Remainder on division by x−k equals p(k).
KeyConcepts.Rule: Evaluate directly rather than perform full division.

KeyConcepts.Title: Factor Theorem
KeyConcepts.Definition: x−k is a factor iff p(k)=0.

KeyConcepts.Title: Rational Zero Theorem
KeyConcepts.Definition: For integer coefficients, any reduced rational root a/b has a dividing constant and b dividing leading coefficient.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Candidates need testing; some roots irrational or complex.

KeyConcepts.Title: Synthetic root testing
KeyConcepts.Definition: Substitute candidate and divide to lower polynomial degree.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Repeat a root to detect multiplicity.

KeyConcepts.Title: Linear factorization
KeyConcepts.Definition: Polynomial over complex numbers factors into degree1 factors counting multiplicity.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Real-coefficient polynomials have nonreal conjugate pairs.

KeyConcepts.Title: Complex conjugate zeros
KeyConcepts.Definition: If coefficients are real and a+bi is a root with b≠0, a−bi also is.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Multiply conjugate factors into real quadratic.

KeyConcepts.Title: Descartes' Rule of Signs
KeyConcepts.Definition: Positive real zero count equals sign changes of p(x), or less by an even integer.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Negative real zero count uses sign changes of p(−x).

KeyConcepts.Title: Polynomial from zeros
KeyConcepts.Definition: Multiply (x−r) factors and solve scale from a known point.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Repeated roots use powers and nonreal roots paired for real coefficients.

KeyConcepts.Title: Polynomial volume model
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use only positive physical roots and correct units.

SummaryPoints: Remainder at k is p(k), factor iff remainder0.
Rational candidates are possibilities, not certified zeros.
Nonreal roots occur in conjugate pairs for real polynomials.
Descartes gives sign-change bounds, not exact counts.
Volume model roots must satisfy positive dimensions.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating each Rational Zero Theorem candidate as an actual root.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It is only a finite list to test.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Forgetting complex conjugates in real-coefficient polynomial.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Nonreal zeros must come in conjugate pairs.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating Descartes possible count as actual count.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Counts decrease by even integers and complex roots may exist.
